bug_semantics: The withdrawn report alleged that, after beginning an OAuth sign-in and reaching an OTP challenge, an attacker could alter the attempt request's authentication strategy (for example, swap an email-code attempt to another factor) and have the server complete authentication without the correct code. The public clerk-js 5.88.0 UI does send the factor strategy and entered code to the Frontend API, but that client-controlled request is not an authentication trust boundary; the alleged bypass requires the server to accept a strategy that was not valid for the sign-in attempt. The CNA later rejected CVE-2025-63700 because further investigation established that this was not a security issue.
flaw_origin: No verified flaw exists in the audited repository. The allegation depended on improper state/factor validation by Clerk's non-public Frontend API backend, while clerk/javascript only constructs and sends the client request. The relevant client request behavior predates 5.88.0 and was unchanged by that release, and the authoritative CVE record plus Clerk's first-party vulnerability history state that the report was investigated, withdrawn, and never a real vulnerability.
evidence: Authoritative lifecycle: fetch https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2025-63700 and inspect cveMetadata plus containers.cna.rejectedReasons. The record is state REJECTED, dateRejected 2025-12-23, and says: 'Further investigation showed that it was not a security issue.' NVD's https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-63700 reports the same Rejected status and reason.

First-party disposition: in https://clerk.com/articles/clerk-security-how-we-protect-your-users, section 'Subsequent disclosures, 2025 to 2026', Clerk states that CVE-2025-63700 was a disputed external report, was rejected as 'not a security issue', and 'was never a real vulnerability.' The article's actual vulnerability table contains no CVE-2025-63700 fix.

Original advisory boundary: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3mm3-wfpv-q85g records @clerk/clerk-js <= 5.88.0, 'Patched versions: None', publication 2025-11-20, and update 2025-11-21. The bundle likewise has first_patched_version null. This predates the CNA's 2025-12-23 rejection and explains why the stale GHSA still describes the allegation without a patch.

Release boundary in the clone: `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short) %(objectname) %(*objectname) %(*authordate:iso-strict)' refs/tags/@clerk/clerk-js@5.87.0 refs/tags/@clerk/clerk-js@5.88.0 refs/tags/@clerk/clerk-js@5.89.0` peels the release tags to 6a1fb13a389b2b97db286539f0e9a7ef018ea5ab (5.87.0), c3facf1d1877261c01be5a446458f37e75c6d354 (5.88.0, 2025-08-21), and 3cb634c4a9431a4680350351ffc1516b99e4157e (5.89.0, 2025-08-26). `git show @clerk/clerk-js@5.89.0:packages/clerk-js/CHANGELOG.md` contains no security fix for this allegation; its OTP change is an input-widget rework.

No 5.88 BIC: `git diff --name-status @clerk/clerk-js@5.87.0 @clerk/clerk-js@5.88.0 -- packages/clerk-js/src/core/resources/SignIn.ts packages/clerk-js/src/ui/components/SignIn` shows no change to SignIn.ts; only SignInAccountSwitcher.tsx and SignIn/index.tsx changed, both for unrelated session-task navigation. `git diff @clerk/clerk-js@5.87.0 @clerk/clerk-js@5.88.0 -- packages/clerk-js/CHANGELOG.md` lists captcha, an OAuth immediate-redirect allowlist entry, billing, session-task routing, passkey visibility, and navigation changes, not OTP verification acceptance.

Client-path reconstruction: `git show @clerk/clerk-js@5.88.0:packages/clerk-js/src/ui/components/SignIn/SignInFactorOneCodeForm.tsx` shows the UI calling `attemptFirstFactor({ strategy: props.factor.strategy, code })`; `git show @clerk/clerk-js@5.88.0:packages/clerk-js/src/core/resources/SignIn.ts` shows attemptFirstFactor posting those parameters to action `attempt_first_factor`. This proves only that the browser identifies the attempted factor, not that the server accepts a mismatched or unprepared factor.

History cross-check: `git log -L 182,199:packages/clerk-js/src/core/resources/SignIn.ts @clerk/clerk-js@5.88.0` traces the generic attempt_first_factor POST through 2024/2023/2022 and back to the public-source import 8b00a66c18924a2a99afdb3539bd6663d68eb673 (parent 679ab0e0054250cf9269d28b097cac043ac761a1) on 2022-02-04. That commit is not selected as a BIC because the CNA/vendor evidence establishes that the request construction is not a vulnerability. With no true BIC, direct parent absence and BIC commit-object AI attribution cannot truthfully be asserted.
reasoning: The report's proposed attack crosses the browser/server boundary: changing a browser request is always possible, so a bypass exists only if the Frontend API fails to bind an OTP attempt to the prepared factor and sign-in state. The public SDK at 5.88.0 passes the UI-selected factor strategy and code to that API, but contains no server-side authentication decision. Git diff shows 5.88.0 did not introduce the relevant request path, and git log -L shows the generic path existed years earlier. There is no closing patch or first patched package version; 5.89.0's OTP work only changes the input UI. Most decisively, on 2025-12-23 the CNA withdrew the CVE after determining it was not a security issue, and Clerk's first-party history says it was never a real vulnerability. Selecting the 2022 request helper, the 5.88.0 release commit, or any later change as a BIC would therefore violate the protocol's requirement for the smallest commit that first wrote genuinely vulnerable lines. Since no true BIC exists, there is no parent-absence claim and no BIC commit object on which an AI marker may be judged. EVIDENCE_GAP is used rather than NOT_AI because a closed NOT_AI verdict requires a real BIC; it is used rather than BLOCKED because the repository and public lifecycle are accessible, but the reachable evidence does not establish any vulnerability to attribute.
remaining_gap: A closed AI/non-AI attribution would require a reproducible authentication bypass plus the actual code and history of the server-side factor/state validation that caused and fixed it. No such reproducer, vulnerable backend line, fix commit, or patched version is present in the cited report or public repository, and the CNA/vendor instead affirmatively concluded that the report was not a security issue. Consequently there is no defensible BIC, parent-absence proof, fix SHA, or BIC-only AI marker to record.
